notes: they came is one added unit under rule 2: a supplied subject pronoun and a supplied lexical verb standing together and doing one office in a clause whose Hebrew writes neither (rule 20), headed on came.

מִתַּחַת is a compound of two prepositions in which neither morpheme carries content the other lacks, so it heads on the governing morpheme standing first (rule 23); the לְ before the bare place name keeps nothing (rule 40).

out of Mizpah is divided with out completing the lexeme of יָצָא, which went alone does not write, and of going to מִן; the competing reading gives מִן the whole out of under rule 24 and leaves the verb a bare went.
